AI safety scholar Roman Yampolskiy joins Joe Rogan for episode 2345 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Yampolskiy has warned for years that super smart machines cannot be kept in check. His talks with Rogan rank among the show's most grave.

Yampolskiy lays out why a mind far past ours would slip each cage we build. He walks through the ends such a mind could bring and the slim odds he grants us. Rogan asks what rules could still help. Listeners get the dark case in a clear voice. The library keeps the episode as a record of his stated warnings.
podcast-joerogan-5dDF0c7cy5k:
Astronaut Terry Virts talks quantum mechanics with Rogan in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience. Virts flew in space and commanded the International Space Station, so he brings a pilot's plain speech to a subject famous for confusing everyone.

The two work through the odd rules of the quantum world, where particles act like waves and outcomes come in chances. Virts ties the physics to what he saw from orbit and how a crew lives above Earth. Rogan asks the questions a curious layman would ask. The segment makes deep physics feel like a story told by a man who has been up there.
podcast-joerogan-kmB8_DNeg5k:
Robert Greene and Aubrey Marcus share episode 464 of the Joe Rogan Experience, an early-days pairing. Greene wrote The 48 Laws of Power, the cold-eyed manual of strategy read in boardrooms and locker rooms alike. Marcus, founder of Onnit, was building his name on the examined, optimized life.

The two teachers work over power, seduction, and the laws of human nature with a young Rogan as host. Greene speaks in historical parables while Marcus answers from the gym and the boardroom. The episode is a compact power seminar from the show's rougher years, with two guests who later became fixtures.
